title: Cross-model semantic anchor QC runner and drift signal synthesis
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable offline QC runner that synthesizes drift signals and runs cross-model semantic-anchor validations against tiered golden sets. This runner is intended to power nightly signal generation for the Console drift dashboards, provide reproducible offline metrics for PR-level checks, and produce compact delta reports used by the alerting pipeline. The scope includes dataset curation tooling, a metric suite (ranking and embedding-level), integration with existing telemetry exports, and ops runbooks for threshold calibration.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly job produces a per-model JSON report containing recall@1/5/10, MRR, cosine-similarity-distribution statistics, embedding norm histogram deltas, and KS-test p-values for drift compared to the previous 7-day baseline.
Runner can run end-to-end on a downsampled prod corpus in <= 90 minutes with default config and is parameterizable for larger runs.
Generated reports are wired into the Console drift view and produce alerts when configurable thresholds are crossed (example thresholds documented).
A GitHub Action or CI job using the runner can be triggered for model PRs to produce a simplified delta report (text/markdown) attached to PRs.
Documentation and a short runbook for on-call including recommended thresholds and false-positive mitigation steps are published.
Unit and integration tests cover generator, metric calculators, and report serializer with deterministic seeds for synthetic probes.
implementation_notes: Design tiered golden sets: 'anchor-core' (stable human-labeled pairs), 'anchor-broad' (large auto-curated pairs), 'stability-probe' (synthetic paraphrases and noise-injection).

Metric suite: ranking metrics (recall@k, MRR), calibration metrics (expected calibration error on cosine bins), distribution metrics (KL divergence on similarity histograms), and stability probes (embedding norm drift, nearest-neighbor churn).

Signal synthesis: implement perturbation operators (token-level synonym swaps, dropout noise, phrase reordering) to generate controlled synthetic drift. Provide seed files so nightly runs are reproducible.
Compute/latency tuning: use batched embedding computation with cached prefixes where applicable; expose batch_size/worker_concurrency as parameters for the orchestrator.
Storage: store reports in S3-like buckets partitioned by model/version/date and emit a compact index for Console ingestion. Use ndjson for line-delimited per-sample outputs.
Integration: add an ingestion hook that writes summary metrics to telemetry (metrics namespace 'embed.qc') and posts a structured message to the Console ingestion topic.
CI hook: lightweight runner mode that samples 1k anchors and emits PR comment with top 5 regressions and a histogram image link.
Backward compatibility: runner must accept legacy golden set formats for a migration window and log any conversion warnings.
risks: Sampling bias: small nightly samples might not surface rare regressions—need stratified sampling by customer/region/model bucket.
Cost vs coverage: full-corpus runs are expensive on large models; we must provide sensible defaults and guardrails to avoid runaway bills.
Alert fatigue: naive thresholds will create noisy alerts; will require a calibration period and suppression rules tied to releases/rollouts.
Data sensitivity: golden sets derived from customer text require vetting and PII scrubbing—policy sign-off might be needed for some corpora.
Compatibility: some older models use pre-normalized embeddings; comparison code must handle per-model preprocessing differences.
